methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); automaker signals

pit_profile.why: Ford Motor Company 'develops and delivers innovative, must-have Ford trucks, sport utility vehicles, commercial vans and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles, along with connected services'; among its risk factors, 'Industry sales volume can be volatile and could decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, public health emergency, or significant geopolitical event' and 'Ford’s results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States' (its own FY2023 10-K); EV is live (from about 2020) and its 10-K risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Ford

theme_watch.reason: Live: Ford's own FY2023 10-K, under 'Ford’s results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States.', says 'A shift in consumer preferences away from larger, more profitable vehicles with internal combustion engines (including trucks and utilities) to electric or other vehicles in our portfolio that may be less profitable could result in an adverse effect on our financial condition or results of operations.' Its business: 'develops and delivers innovative, must-have Ford trucks, sport utility vehicles, commercial vans and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles, along with connected services'. The stock trades at 5.6x FY24E — a discount to its own history. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (EV) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing electric-vehicle substitution of Ford's combustion-engine profits specifically.

classification.quality_note: Ford Motor Company 'develops and delivers innovative, must-have Ford trucks, sport utility vehicles, commercial vans and cars, and Lincoln luxury vehicles, along with connected services'; among its risk factors, 'Industry sales volume can be volatile and could decline if there is a financial crisis, recession, public health emergency, or significant geopolitical event' and 'Ford’s results are dependent on sales of larger, more profitable vehicles, particularly in the United States' (its own FY2023 10-K); EV is live (from about 2020) and its 10-K risk factor puts it on the watch list: company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Ford. durable franchise (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B 1.18x; +12% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.00; conservative 2yr +46%.

BEAR.desc: EPS -69.0%/yr (worst year FY14-FY23, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +6.1%/yr (Q2 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +6.3%/yr (FY14-FY23 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +128.5%/yr (best 2-yr run FY14-FY23); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: F (retrospective, 2024-08-23) ◐ WATCHLIST — Ratio B 1.18x (91.1% downside to Bear $1 / +77.5% upside to Bull $20) | Adj composite 2.71 vs market 1.71: gap +1.00 [UNDERVALUED] | +12% above the EPP floor $10 (5x FY24E $2.01) | Conservative 2-yr case: +46.2% total (+23.1%/yr) | At 5.6x FY24E the 15% hurdle price $15 sits at or below the BASE case; wholesale units +2.1% in Q2 2024, forward revenues +6.3% (no Q3 2024 revenue guide, Q2 2024 revenue as reported); EV is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
